definition: An external object that satisfies human wants and has both use-value and exchange-value

contrasts.differential: Commodity is a product with use-value, money is the universal equivalent form
Commodity is a product for exchange, capital is self-valorizing value

definition: The qualitative aspect of a commodity that satisfies a particular human need through its physical properties

contrasts.differential: Use-value is qualitative and particular, exchange-value is quantitative and universal

definition: The quantitative proportion in which use-values of one kind exchange for use-values of another kind

contrasts.differential: Exchange-value abstracts from quality, use-value is defined by quality
Exchange-value is the form of appearance of value, value is the substance

definition: The socially necessary abstract labour time objectified in a commodity

contrasts.differential: Value is abstract social substance, use-value is concrete material quality
Value is the essence, price is its monetary expression which can deviate from value

definition: Human labour considered as expenditure of human labour-power in general, abstracted from its concrete form

contrasts.differential: Abstract labour creates value, concrete labour creates use-value

definition: Labour in its specific useful form that produces a particular use-value

contrasts.differential: Concrete labour produces use-value, abstract labour produces value

definition: The difference between the value created by labour-power and the value of labour-power itself, appropriated by capital

contrasts.differential: Surplus-value comes from unpaid labour beyond necessary labour time
Surplus-value is the essence, profit is its phenomenal form

definition: The capacity to labour, which the worker sells as a commodity; its use-value is the source of value

contrasts.differential: Labour-power is the capacity sold, labour is the actual activity of production

definition: Value in process, self-valorizing value that passes through the circuit M-C-M' to produce surplus-value

contrasts.differential: Capital is money that breeds money through production, money is merely means of circulation
Capital is value in motion, commodity is value at rest in a product

definition: The universal equivalent form of value, the commodity that serves as measure of value and means of circulation

contrasts.differential: Money is the universal equivalent, commodity is a particular product
Money circulates commodities, capital valorizes itself through production

definition: The mystification whereby social relations between people appear as relations between things
The portion of capital invested in means of production whose value is transferred unchanged to the product

contrasts.differential: Constant capital transfers existing value, variable capital creates new value including surplus-value

definition: The portion of capital invested in labour-power that creates new value greater than its own cost

contrasts.differential: Variable capital produces surplus-value, constant capital merely transfers its value

definition: The material conditions of production including raw materials, instruments, and fixed capital

contrasts.differential: Means of production are dead labour objectified, labour-power is living labour capacity

definition: The social relations people enter into in the process of production, determining class structure

contrasts.differential: Relations of production are social forms, forces of production are material capacities

definition: The material productive capacities of society including labour-power, tools, and knowledge

contrasts.differential: Forces of production are material capacities, relations of production are their social form

definition: The conversion of surplus-value back into capital, the reproduction of capital on an expanding scale

contrasts.differential: Accumulation expands capital, simple reproduction merely maintains it

definition: The historical process of separating producers from means of production that created the preconditions for capital

contrasts.differential: Primitive accumulation is the historical precondition, accumulation is the ongoing process of capital

definition: The extraction of surplus-value from labour through the difference between value created and wages paid
The estrangement of workers from their product, process, species-being, and fellow workers under capital
